correctness.rationale: The result explicitly fixes the eight integral rays and twelve smooth complete maximal cones, so its quantifiers are over exactly this fan family. Independently reconstructed all 18 two-dimensional wall relations from two incident maximal cones by exact symbolic linear algebra and verified their 18 anticanonical degrees match the complete displayed wall table; the six zero exclusions are exactly the nonconstant types. For the four remaining ray convex-hull tests, linear supporting functionals reduce each to two strict inequalities ut<v, wt<z for t in (-1,1). The stated E predicate is equivalent by same-sign and opposite-sign one-dimensional half-interval intersection, including zero coefficient and equality boundaries. Four other rays are permanently exposed by first-coordinate supporting functionals with perturbations. Independent linear-program primal convex-hull tests on representative integer quadruples agreed with all four arithmetic ray tests; the original checker tests a finite 625-grid, not an infinite proof. The two easy E constraints yield d>=-|a|-1 and d<=|c|. Substitution (0,m,m,0) verifies E and wall nonzero for m>=2; max absolute wall degree 2m proves toric separation. Invoking Ito–Zeng–Zeng’s published canonical ray+curve criterion is an explicitly stated external mathematical premise; this run independently verified its algebraic fan specialization but could not independently reread the complete newly posted original theorem text.

originality.rationale: PASS, carefully qualified. The newly posted general criterion and all-integer open classification question in Ito–Zeng–Zeng (arXiv:2610.22279) are acknowledged as prior. A public open-problem extract explicitly quotes their question for unrestricted Z_double_prime_13(a,b,c,d), while their paper abstract promises a broad fan criterion and special nonprojective examples, not this ten-integer-test table. Fujino–Sato arXiv:2412.02392 supplies the actual fan and projectivity but not canonical tensor generation. The arithmetized 4D parameter classification, finite band and torically distinguished infinite family were not found in the inspected material. The Ito source full text remained inaccessible despite lawful attempts, so exact coverage is a serious residual risk; no absolute novelty is claimed.
residual_risks: Original full Ito–Zeng–Zeng paper is too recent to inspect through available preprint routes in this run; authoritative confirmation of the exact ray+curve formulation and exhaustive prior family statements remains open.

The family is pairwise distinct as TORIC varieties, not proven nonisomorphic as abstract varieties; finite d-band is only necessary.
